question_text: [Experiment Design & A/B Testing - Q14] In online A/B testing, how does the CUPED (Controlled-experiment Using Pre-Experiment Data) method increase statistical power?

options.text: By doubling the sample size via synthetic bootstrap samples
By using pre-experiment baseline covariates correlated with the outcome metric to subtract unexplained variance, narrowing confidence intervals
By converting two-tailed hypothesis tests into one-tailed tests
By removing users who convert in the control group

answer_explanation: CUPED utilizes pre-experiment metric values Y_pre as a control variate: Y_cuped = Y - theta * (Y_pre - E[Y_pre]), drastically reducing variance and required sample size.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: CUPED utilizes pre-experiment metric values Y_pre as a control variate: Y_cuped = Y - theta * (Y_pre - E[Y_pre]), drastically reducing variance and required sample size.
